vulnerability_summary: libcrux-sha3 portable incremental SHAKE dropped the unread suffix of a partially squeezed RATE block before the next squeeze call, producing incorrect output when a non-final call requested a non-RATE-aligned length.
causality: Human commit f34493bb7bb2359d83e6d8f45bcaa3fcf8a12400 first introduced the underlying no-output-buffer design: a partial squeeze returned only the requested prefix, set sponge=true, and the next call permuted before preserving the unread suffix. Human commit 470fc6004f48be9a64a32b7f09e1eb557f6c83e0 made that XOF implementation working and public, and human commit bf2b9009a05138d363549fa73628254f6e6a59ad introduced the exact affected Shake128Xof/Shake256Xof API names. Human commits 3ccdc1d0af4560c2ba5f3b27484fc595b41c04c3 and 276794b8f11c49b6b3f5425093c5dd06be99ae24 retained that behavior. Claude-coauthored commit 5ad079d4e4a7b8ec9902f0b860ae53d56c27368a fixes the distinct RUSTSEC-2026-0074 single-call >RATE first-block skip. For the RUSTSEC-2026-0207 sub-RATE path it only changes the guard from out_len <= RATE to the semantically equivalent blocks == 0; the prefix extraction, next-call permutation, sponge transition, and lack of an output buffer remain unchanged. Its added multi-call test uses three exactly RATE-sized chunks and is test-only evidence for the prior fix. The commit therefore supplies fix-only and test-only AI evidence, with no material vulnerable reimplementation of the partial-chunk path. Human commit aab63a96c51ef70f7a13303b67658cdf70665ebe is the first real fix: it adds squeeze_buf/squeeze_pos, drains unread bytes before permuting, and adds partial-chunk regressions. That commit is an ancestor of final merge e9ecdd274ea36e40c90acb21ccea6b5f6955a6b8 (PR #1389), released in libcrux-sha3 0.0.10.

evidence.test_only_change: bug1_xof_squeeze_multi_call_consistency compares one 504-byte squeeze with three 168-byte RATE-aligned calls; it never exercises a partial chunk.

behavioral_reproduction.test: SHAKE128 one-shot 200 bytes versus incremental squeeze calls of 100 + 100 bytes
